Students & graduates

Your first engineering job, ready from day one

Free practical training in your discipline, then the chance to join a partner company that pays you from your first day.

  1. Home
  2. Students & graduates

Sound familiar?

What gets in the way

  • No experience, no job

    Entry-level roles ask for experience, and it’s hard to get experience without a first job.

  • Theory, but not the tools

    University gives you strong foundations, but rarely the tools and ways of working a real engineering team uses.

  • Unclear expectations

    It’s hard to know what companies actually expect from a junior engineer on day one.

  • Fear of unpaid work

    Some programmes ask you to work for free, or to pay for a course with no clear route to a job.

The programme

What the programme is

  • Practical training

    8–10 weeks, part-time and mostly remote, on the tools and ways of working partner companies use. You can join while you finish your degree.

  • A mentor at your side

    An engineer from our team supports you through the training and stays with you during your first project at the company.

  • A paid first role

    Partner companies meet the participants and decide who to hire. If one hires you, you join under its contract and are paid from day one.

Who it’s for

Can you apply?

  • You are in the final year of a bachelor’s or master’s degree, or graduated in the last 3 years.
  • Your degree is in a technical or scientific subject, or you can show the skills another way.
  • You have working English, plus Italian or Spanish at the level the company’s workplace needs.
  • You can follow the part-time foundation phase on your cohort’s dates.
  • You can work in the country of the role; we check this when you meet the companies.
  • There is no age limit.

How it works

What happens, step by step

  1. 01

    Application

    You apply with your CV, your discipline track, the country you want to work in and your languages. We check that you’re eligible.

  2. 02

    Selection

    A short call, a practical task for your track that you do from home, and an interview with an engineer. You get a decision and written feedback at every stage you reach.

    Typical duration
    4–6 weeks

  3. 03

    Foundation phase

    About 10–15 hours a week, mostly remote, with an on-site kick-off, so you can keep studying. It ends with a demo day, where partner companies meet you and make their offers.

    Typical duration
    8–10 weeks, part-time

  4. 04

    Employer project phase

    If a company hires you, you join it as an employee from your first day, on an apprenticeship in Italy or a training contract in Spain, and work on a project in its team with one of our mentors.

    Typical duration
    3–6 months

  5. 05

    Follow-up

    We stay in touch with you and your company through your first year.

    Typical duration
    12 months

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to pay anything?

No, never. There is no fee, no deposit and nothing to repay, in any situation. Partner companies fund the programme.

Am I paid?

You’re paid from your first day at the company. If a partner company hires you, you join it as an employee, usually on an apprenticeship (apprendistato) in Italy or a training contract (contrato formativo) in Spain, with at least the pay its collective agreement sets. The foundation phase before it is free training, not work.

Can I do it while I’m studying?

Yes. The foundation phase is part-time, about 10 to 15 hours a week, and mostly remote, so you can join in your final year without pausing your degree.

Who can apply?

Final-year bachelor’s or master’s students, and graduates within 3 years of finishing, with a technical or scientific degree or skills you can show another way. There is no age limit. Each cohort runs one track, software & IT, cybersecurity, or mechanical & industrial engineering.

How does selection work?

After you apply, we check that you’re eligible and have a short call with you. Then you do a practical task for your track from home and have an interview with an engineer. Everyone in a cohort gets the same task, and people, not software, score it against the same criteria. You get a decision and short written feedback at every stage you reach.

What if I’m not placed?

No job is guaranteed, and we won’t pretend otherwise. Partner companies decide who to hire. If none hires you, you keep your certificate, get written feedback, and have priority for 12 months for our graduate roles and the next cohort. You’re also free to apply anywhere else.

Do I have to stay, or repay anything if I leave?

No. We never ask you to repay your training, and you don’t have to accept an offer. We also recommend that companies don’t add a stay clause to a first job.

Which language is the training in?

Placeholder, to be confirmed: the language of instruction is still being decided, and each cohort will state it before applications open. Either way, you need working English, plus Italian or Spanish at the level your future workplace needs.

Is this an unpaid internship?

No. You only work for a company as its employee, under its contract and paid from your first day.
